subject: Hosted API: marketplace billing vs direct — proposed commit & surcharge handling
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finova.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Question on per-token tiers + marketplace invoicing

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Finova's ML team is excited. Procurement looped me in with a couple of practical questions before we can move to a PO:

1) We plan to commit to $250k of hosted API spend over 12 months. Can you confirm the per-token volume discount schedule at that commit level (e.g., discounts at 250M / 1B tokens)?
2) Procurement insists on billing through AWS Marketplace for contractual/controls reasons. The marketplace listing shows a separate "service fee" — how does Redwood handle discounts if we buy via marketplace versus direct billing? Are discounts applied to marketplace line items or only to direct invoices?

We need a short, explicit answer we can give to procurement. Appreciate a one-page summary if possible.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Torres
Director, Platform Engineering — Finova Labs

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finova.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on per-token tiers + marketplace invoicing

Sam—

Short answer up front: we can support your $250k commit with our mid-tier volume discounts, but marketplace billing introduces an additional pass-through fee that changes the invoiced amount unless we make an explicit crediting arrangement. Key points below (TL;DR at top):

TL;DR:
- Commit tiers: $250k/year typically aligns to the 3-tier schedule (Tier A: 0-250M tokens; Tier B: 250M-1B; Tier C: 1B+). Effective blended discount for a $250k commit is ~12–14% off list per-token rates (example in attachment).
- Marketplace: AWS/GCP/Azure typically add a 7–12% marketplace surcharge. That surcharge is outside Redwood's list rates and, by default, reduces the net discount to you unless Redwood issues a marketplace credit.

Details and options we can offer for Finova Labs:
1) Direct-parity option: Redwood issues a marketplace credit equal to the marketplace fee for the first 12 months so your effective cost matches the direct-billing net price. Requires an amendment and a committed spend window (we can use your $250k commit).
2) Shared-surcharge option: Redwood covers up to 50% of the marketplace fee for the contract term; remaining surcharge shows as a separate marketplace line item on invoices.
3) No-parity option: list pricing applies; marketplace fee is fully passed through.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with worked examples (est. token volumes) and a one-page memo on marketplace mechanics. If procurement wants marketplace invoicing due to internal controls, option (1) is the cleanest from their POV — we issue a credit in our billing system and they are still billed via AWS with a separate line for the marketplace fee but net cost is equivalent.

Next step: Can you put procurement on a thread and share their PO timing/requirements? I can draft an amendment (DocuSign) that covers crediting or partial crediting.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing_commit_options.xlsx (spreadsheet), marketplace_fee_memo.pdf (doc)

From: procurement@finova.com
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@finova.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on per-token tiers + marketplace invoicing

Neha, Sam —

Procurement here. A few constraints so we're explicit:
- We require invoice lineage via AWS Marketplace (we can't accept direct invoices due to controls).
- PO will reference an annual commitment and we prefer discounts be visible as a reduction on the marketplace line item (not as vendor credits routed separately).
- Standard timeline for PO to execution is ~2 weeks after we have a signed SOW/amendment and finalized taxes/marketplace SKU.

Is Redwood able to represent discounted pricing directly on the AWS SKU (so the marketplace invoice shows discounted unit price) rather than relying on a separate vendor credit? If not, we need to document the credit flow for our auditors.

Thanks,
Procurement Team — Finova Labs

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: marketplace billing question — proposed approach for Finova (internal)

Team — forwarding Finova procurement. They want discounts visible on the marketplace SKU (auditor-friendly). AWS typically doesn't let partners alter the marketplace service fee, but we have two pragmatic paths:

A) SKU-level discounting: negotiate a reduced per-unit price when we list the SKU in AWS Marketplace — this requires a marketplace price update and can take 5–10 business days to appear. Once updated, procurement sees discounted unit costs on invoices. Downside: Marketplace contract amendments and evidence required.

B) Crediting flow (what I suggested externally): Redwood bills net on our system and issues a marketplace fee credit to offset the surcharge for the first 12 months (or X% share). That credit shows up as a Redwood credit memo rather than a Marketplace unit price change. Auditors accept credit memos if documented well, but it is more awkward for procurement teams who prefer everything on-marketplace.

Recommendation: Offer SKU-level discounting for the 12-month commit if Finova signs the amendment and commits to $250k. That preserves their procurement requirements and gives them the clean marketplace invoice. We should also build in a fallback credit workflow in case marketplace listing changes don't propagate in time.

Attached: a draft amendment and the pricing spreadsheet (pricing_commit_options.xlsx, amendment_draft.docx).

Questions: 1) Karthik — how long to update the SKU pricing if legal OKs the amendment? 2) Rishi — can we afford full parity credit for 12 months instead of SKU-change if the marketplace path is slow? What are the arithmetic impacts on margin?

-Neha

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: marketplace billing question — proposed approach for Finova (internal)

Neha — thanks for the thoughtful breakdown. My thoughts:

- Prefer SKU-level discount (Option A) where feasible: it solves procurement friction and reduces admin overhead for finance.
- If SKU change timing > 7 business days we should automatically apply a temporary credit equal to the estimated marketplace fee for month 1–3, then reconcile after SKU goes live. Cap the temporary credit at $25k to limit risk.
- Margin math: offering SKU parity for 12 months on a $250k commit (~$250k blended) will reduce gross margin by roughly 8–10% on that book of business vs net list if we absorb the marketplace fee. That's acceptable if Finova is strategic and likely to expand.

Ask legal to prioritize the amendment so karthik can trigger marketplace ops. I'll approve the capped credit fallback. Once we have procurement's PO language I can sign off.

-Rishi

Sam / Procurement —

Thanks for the clarity. Proposal below for Finova Labs (please reply with confirmation or redlines):

Proposal summary:

- SKU-level discount: Redwood will publish a reduced unit price on the AWS Marketplace SKU to reflect the agreed commit-tier discount (est. blended ~13% off list). This will make discounted pricing visible on AWS invoices.
- Marketplace fee handling: If SKU update is not live within 7 business days of signed amendment, Redwood will issue a temporary credit equal to the estimated marketplace fee for months 1–3 (capped at $25k). When SKU is live we will reconcile any over/under credit on the following invoice.
